Worked Example: A $15,000 Personal Loan

Borrow $15,000 at 9% APR. Over 5 years the payment is about $311.38 a month and total interest is about $3,683. Shorten the term to 3 years and the payment rises to about $477.00, but interest drops to about $2,172.

The shorter loan costs about $166 more each month and saves about $1,511 in interest. The right choice depends on what your monthly budget can safely carry.

Comparing Loan Offers

  • Look at APR, not just the interest rate. APR includes certain fees, so it is the better number for comparing lenders.
  • Check for an origination fee. Some lenders deduct it from the amount you receive, so you repay more than you actually get.
  • Ask about prepayment penalties. Most personal loans have none, but confirm before signing.
  • Compare total cost. A lower payment on a longer term often means a higher total cost.

Before You Borrow

Lenders mainly look at your credit history, income and existing debt. A lower debt-to-income ratio and a higher credit score usually mean a lower rate. If you are borrowing for a car or a home, the auto loan calculator and mortgage calculator add the costs specific to those loans.

extra_faqs.q: How is the monthly loan payment calculated?
extra_faqs.a: It uses the amortization formula: payment = P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n), where P is the amount borrowed, r is the monthly rate and n is the number of payments. Each payment covers that month's interest first, then reduces principal.

extra_faqs.q: Is it better to take a shorter loan term?
extra_faqs.a: A shorter term costs less interest overall but raises the monthly payment. If the payment fits your budget comfortably, shorter is usually cheaper; if not, a longer term with extra payments when possible gives flexibility.

extra_faqs.q: What is the difference between APR and interest rate?
extra_faqs.a: The interest rate is the cost of borrowing the principal. APR adds certain lender fees and expresses the total as a yearly rate, which makes offers easier to compare.
